findings.detail: The keying change from `f.name` to `keyOf(f)` is correct and is what fixes two uploads called `export.xlsx` collapsing into one. But `removeFile(name)`, `moveCol(fileName, …)`, `updateCol(fileName, …)` and `getProcessedDataForFile(fileName)` kept their old parameter names while every call site now passes `keyOf(f)` (e.g. `removeFile(keyOf(f))`, `getProcessedDataForFile(keyOf(f))`). A reader — or the next person adding a call site — will reasonably pass `f.name`, which silently returns `[]` from `getProcessedDataForFile` (the `allFiles.find(f => keyOf(f) === fileName)` lookup misses) and produces an empty sheet rather than an error. The regression this PR just fixed is exactly that class of bug.
findings.summary: Per-file helpers still take a param named `name`/`fileName` but now receive an opaque id

findings.detail: The same "drop the file extension to build an output name" step now appears at `components/CleanTool.tsx:98` (`res.fileName.lastIndexOf('.')`), `components/MergeTool.tsx:189` and `components/MergeTool.tsx:207` (same shape, on `f.name`), and `components/SplitterTool.tsx` (`fileData.name.replace(/\.[^/.]+$/, '')` — a third, different implementation added by this PR). The two forms happen to agree on every input I checked (`a.csv`, `archive.tar.gz`, `.gitignore`, no-extension), so there is no bug today. It's worth consolidating because this PR already created the natural home for it — `utils/excelUtils.ts` now exports `uniqueNames` and `safeSheetName`, and all four call sites feed one of those two helpers. Below the code-smells handbook's 15-line duplication threshold, hence low.
findings.summary: Extension-stripping is open-coded in four places across this diff, in two different forms

findings.detail: `mappedCount` counts every non-`-1` entry in `columnMapping`, including the mapping for the key column itself. The auto-map at line 63-79 maps by header name, so `SKU → SKU` is normally present. A user who sets every other column to `-- Ignore --` leaves `mappedCount === 1`, Run is enabled, and `compareDatasets` compares the key column against itself — which matches for every shared key by construction. The result is the same misleading "perfect match on everything" report the guard was added to prevent, just via a narrower path. Not a regression (before this PR the zero-column case produced it too), and the trigger needs deliberate user action, which is why this is low rather than medium.
findings.summary: The "map at least one column" guard counts the key column, so an all-match report is still reachable

findings.detail: `catch(err: any) { if (!finishRun(runId)) return; addLog(...) }` discards the error message when `runId` is no longer the active run. Today that branch is unreachable — the single Run button at line 649 is `disabled={… || status === ProcessingStatus.PROCESSING}`, so a second run can't start and `finishRun` always returns true — so there is no user impact now. But the guard exists precisely to anticipate overlapping runs; the day one becomes possible (an auto-run on settings change, a cancel-and-rerun button), a merge failure becomes a completely silent no-op with the spinner already cleared by the newer run. The success path's equivalent guard is fine because it has an explicit `addLog` for its discard case; the error path has none.
findings.summary: A superseded run's exception returns from `catch` without logging it
